metadata.title: Jauan Jennings - Not practicing Thursday
metadata.description: Jennings (calf) did not participate at practice Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Jennings was estimated as a non-participant on the Vikings' injury report Wednesday after being sidelined in Week 9, and he wasn't able to take the practice field Thursday. Unless he's able to return to practice in some capacity Friday, he'll probably end up missing a second straight game in Week 10, which could leave Myles Price with an expanded role at wideout come Sunday at Green Bay.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings Does Not Practice Again on Thursday
metadata.description: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings (calf) was listed as a non-participant in practice for the second straight day. Jennings' agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said earlier this week that his client's calf injury is not serious and that he expects to play in Week 10 against the Green Bay Packers, but he now must return to the practice field on Friday to avoid being ruled out for a second straight game. The Vikings' passing game was taken hostage by a terrible Carson Wentz at quarterback in Monday night's loss to the Buffalo Bills, but with veteran Kirk Cousins now in the fold, Minnesota is hoping that their offense can now complement one of the best defenses in the NFL. Jennings has been nearly non-existent in his first year with the Vikings as the WR3 behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, catching only six passes for 54 yards and no touchdowns in six games played. The addition of Cousins at the trade deadline on Tuesday should be a boost for the offense for the rest of the season, but Jennings still will not be much more than a deep-league bench stash at wide receiver. If he is active at Lambeau on Sunday, he should be planted on fantasy benches. He is rostered in only 3% of Yahoo leagues.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings (calf) misses practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Jauan Jennings did not practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Jennings missed Week 9 against the Bills. He remains off the fantasy radar when he is healthy.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings - Starts week with DNP
metadata.description: Jennings (calf) was estimated as DNP on Wednesday's practice report.
metadata.analysis: The veteran wideout missed last Monday night's loss to the Bills. If he's unable to play Sunday against the Packers, Tai Felton would be in line to handle WR3 duties for Minnesota behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison. Jennings has six catches for 54 yards across six games this season.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings Hopeful to Play in Week 10
metadata.description: Agent Drew Rosenhaus said on The Pat McAfee Show that Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings (calf) is dealing with a calf strain but is hopeful to return in Week 10 against the division-rival Green Bay Packers. Rosenhaus added that Jennings seems very happy in Minnesota and that it is his belief that he will stay with the Vikings beyond Tuesday's NFL trade deadline. Jennings reportedly turned down a potential trade that was being worked out for the 49ers to reacquire him. Instead, the Niners pivoted and acquired veteran pass-catcher Keenan Allen from the Indianapolis Colts on Tuesday. The 29-year-old has been a non-factor in the Vikings' offense through his six games played so far in 2026, catching only six passes for 54 yards and no touchdowns. However, the addition of veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins should be good news for Jennings, Justin Jefferson, and Jordan Addison in the second half of the season. Target volume is still going to be an issue when Jennings returns in Minnesota, though, and he will probably continue to be a hard-to-trust WR4/5 in fantasy.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings (calf) ruled out Monday
metadata.description: Jauan Jennings has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Bills.
metadata.analysis: Jennings did not practice on Friday or Saturday. He remains off the fantasy radar.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings - Won't play in Week 9
metadata.description: Jennings (calf) has been ruled out for Monday's contest versus the Bills.
metadata.analysis: Per head coach Kevin O'Connell, Jennings suffered a calf injury at Thursday's practice that is serious enough to sideline him for at least one game. Jennings' next chance for game action is Sunday, Nov. 15 in Green Bay, while Tai Felton and Myles Price are in for some offensive snaps this week behind the top WR duo of Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings Ruled Out for Monday Night Against Bills
metadata.description: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings (calf) has been ruled out for Monday night's Week 9 matchup against the Buffalo Bills, according to Will Ragatz. Jennings was limited in Thursday's practice before being downgraded to a nonparticipant Friday. The 29-year-old caught both of his targets for 11 yards during Minnesota's Week 8 loss to the Detroit Lions and has recorded six receptions for 54 yards across six appearances this season. Jennings has been working behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, but his absence could move rookie Tai Felton into the No. 3 receiver role. Felton has caught three passes for 41 yards this season, leaving him with limited demonstrated fantasy production despite the potential increase in playing time. Minnesota will also be without starting quarterback Kyler Murray (hamstring), with Carson Wentz taking over under center against Buffalo.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings - DNP Friday
metadata.description: Jennings (calf) did not participate in Friday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Jennings downgraded his practice participation Friday after being limited in Thursday's session. The wide receiver will likely need to show up in some capacity Saturday for a chance to suit up for Monday night's primetime showdown with the Bills.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings - Limited by calf injury
metadata.description: Jennings (calf) was limited in Thursday's practice.
metadata.analysis: It's a new injury for Jennings, but he has an extra day to recover this week, as the Vikings play the Bills on Monday night. Jennings has six grabs for 54 yards on 10 targets across six games this season and is nowhere near fantasy relevance in his current role.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings Heard 49ers' Plans Before Proposed Trade Fell Through
metadata.description: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings was informed of his potential role with the San Francisco 49ers during a FaceTime conversation about a proposed trade, according to David Lombardi. General manager John Lynch confirmed Thursday that San Francisco could have completed the deal without consulting Jennings but wanted to respect the relationship the organization had built with its former receiver. Head coach Kyle Shanahan previously explained that Jennings expressed satisfaction with his situation in Minnesota during the conversation, prompting the 49ers to abandon the reunion. Jennings spent five seasons playing for San Francisco before joining Minnesota this offseason, where he has struggled to establish himself in the passing attack. The 29-year-old has caught just six of 10 targets for 54 yards without a touchdown across six games, including two receptions for 11 yards against Detroit in Week 8. He remains behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison in the receiving hierarchy, limiting his immediate fantasy appeal in standard redraft leagues.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings - Two grabs in Week 8 loss
metadata.description: Jennings caught both of his targets for 11 yards in Sunday's 19-15 loss to the Lions.
metadata.analysis: The Vikings' third receiver, Jennings ran 20 route on Kyler Murray's 33 dropbacks, playing behind both Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison. Jennings' name has been linked to trade speculation but recently declined a deal to San Francisco after the two teams agreed to trade parameters. Jennings has six grabs for 54 yards on 10 targets across six games this season.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings quiet in Week 8
metadata.description: Jauan Jennings caught both of his targets for 11 yards in the Vikings' 19-15 loss to the Lions in Week 8.
metadata.analysis: Jennings has been minimally involved in the Minnesota passing attack to this point, finishing with under 35 receiving yards in each of his six contests. The wideout remains difficult to trust ahead of a Week 9 contest against the Buffalo Bills.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings declines trade to 49ers
metadata.description: Vikings WR Jauan Jennings reportedly declined a trade that would have sent him back to the San Francisco 49ers.
metadata.analysis: Jennings spent the past five seasons in San Francisco before signing with Minnesota this past offseason. He will remain off the fantasy radar with the Vikings.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings - Declines trade to 49ers
metadata.description: Jennings elected to remain with the Vikings after the team had an agreement in place to move him to the 49ers earlier in the week in a deal that was contingent on the receiver's approval, Jay Glazer reported on "Fox NFL Sunday."
metadata.analysis: According to Glazer, Jennings would have returned to San Francisco if he hopped on a FaceTime call with the 49ers brass to confirm his willingness to rejoin his former squad, but the wideout instead elected to stick around in Minnesota. San Francisco has obvious gaps in its receiving corps due to injuries, and Jennings' familiarity with head coach Kyle Shanahan's system would have made him a natural choice to help strengthen the position group. However, Jennings also left on somewhat acrimonious terms due to his contract situation before becoming a free agent, which may have been a factor in his decision not to sign off on the trade. He'll be active for Sunday's game in Detroit but has struggled to carve out much volume in the passing attack thus far, notching just four receptions for 43 yards on eight targets through his first five appearances with Minnesota.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings Blocks a Trade Back to the 49ers
metadata.description: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings reportedly opposed a return to the San Francisco 49ers, causing a proposed trade between the two teams to fall apart, according to Ari Meirov. The 29-year-old signed a one-year deal with Minnesota in May after spending six seasons in San Francisco, where he caught 55 passes for 643 yards and nine touchdowns in 2025. His production has dropped considerably with the Vikings, recording just four receptions for 43 yards on eight targets across five games. Jennings has struggled to establish himself in a receiving corps led by Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, prompting speculation about his future ahead of the November 10 trade deadline. While a reunion with San Francisco now appears unlikely, a move elsewhere remains possible. For fantasy managers, Jennings remains difficult to roster in standard leagues given his limited involvement in Minnesota's passing attack.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings Is a Trade Bet, Not a Production Add
metadata.description: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings is a trade bet, not a production add -- trade rumors, not production, drive the waiver case. He caught two of three targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 16-10 victory over the Indianapolis Colts, his best receiving performance of the season, but he played just 33 offensive snaps (56%), down from 49 (69%) in Week 5. He has managed only four receptions for 43 yards on eight targets through five appearances, with Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and T.J. Hockenson commanding more prominent roles. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport named Jennings a potential trade candidate on October 13, suggesting a return to San Francisco could make sense. No deal has materialized, so Jennings has little immediate appeal against the Detroit Lions in Week 8. Stash him in leagues with at least 14 teams only if you'll gamble on a change of scenery before the November 10 trade deadline.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings totals 34 yards Sunday
metadata.description: Jauan Jennings caught 2-of-3 targets for 34 yards in the Vikings 16-10 win over the Colts.
metadata.analysis: Jennings nearly caught a long touchdown from Kyler Murray in the second quarter. He remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings - Produces 34 yards in Week 7 win
metadata.description: Jennings caught two of three targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Colts.
metadata.analysis: The veteran wideout entered Week 7 with just two catches for nine yards across four games, so this counts as a breakout game for Jennings. He's running plenty of routes alongside Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison at receiver, but Jennings is deep down the list for targets in Minnesota. He's not a recommended fantasy play for next Sunday against the Lions' leaky secondary.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings a Potential Deep-League Stash Amid Trade Buzz
metadata.description: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings has had almost no impact on his team's offense so far in 2026, catching just two passes for nine yards on five targets in four games. The 29-year-old signed with Minnesota in free agency over the offseason, but he's been buried on the team's depth chart behind wideouts Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison. For the time being, Jennings should not be on the radar of fantasy managers. However, there's been some recent buzz that the veteran wideout could be a trade candidate, specifically to his former team, the San Francisco 49ers. Jennings was a productive player for San Francisco in 2025, hauling in 55 receptions for 643 yards and nine touchdowns on 90 targets across 15 games. If Jennings is traded to the 49ers or another wide receiver-needy team, his fantasy value could skyrocket. In deeper leagues, Jennings could be worth stashing off the waiver wire ahead of the NFL's early November trade deadline.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings Could be Traded to 49ers
metadata.description: After leaving the team this offseason, Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings could be on the San Francisco 49ers' radar. According to Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio, signing veteran Odell Beckham Jr. could be a warning to Jennings, who has caught just two passes for nine yards in five games. Jennings appeared frustrated on the sideline after Myles Price fumbled and yelled at head coach Kevin O'Connell during Week 5's 23-13 win over the New Orleans Saints. If Jennings is traded before this season's trade deadline, the 49ers seem like a likely destination. They've dealt with numerous injuries to their wide receiver room, including Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring), De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle), Ricky Pearsall (knee), and Demarcus Robinson (ankle). Fantasy managers should keep an eye on this situation, as Jennings could be a fantasy-relevant option if he's moved to a team like the 49ers.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings Worth Stashing Amidst Trade Rumors
metadata.description: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings has not been able to find much success with his new team. Heading into the Week 6 bye, Jennings has recorded two receptions for nine yards with zero touchdowns. The Vikings were without Jordan Addison (hamstring) this past weekend, and Jennings still only managed one target. Recently, Ian Rapoport mentioned that Jennings is a name to watch ahead of the trade deadline. He hinted that the San Francisco 49ers could be a potential fit, given their history with Jennings and a need for another wide receiver. Fantasy managers who are willing to be patient with Jennings should consider stashing him, given recent trade rumors.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings: 49ers team to monitor
metadata.description: NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reports Jauan Jennings "would be a name for me to keep an eye on" for the 49ers.
metadata.analysis: Jennings has been disappointing to start the season with the Vikings. A reunion with the 49ers could be a possibility as their wide receiver room remains banged up.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings Could be Hot Name on the Trade Market
metadata.description: The NFL Network's Ian Rapoport said on The Pat McAfee Show on Tuesday that there are a lot of trade conversations going on around the NFL right now, and a name that he has been wondering about is Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings. Rapoport expects Jennings' name to heat up over the next couple of days and weeks, especially after the San Francisco 49ers lost another receiver in veteran Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring) in the Week 5 win over the division-rival Seattle Seahawks on Sunday. The Niners let the 29-year-old Jennings walk in free agency last offseason, but they could be interested in a reunion with the former seventh-rounder because of all of the injuries to their WR corps early in the 2026 season. Even with star Vikings receiver Justin Jefferson missing Week 4 due to an ankle injury, Jennings has had a very minimal impact with the Vikes through four contests, catching two of five targets for only nine yards. A move back to the Bay Area might be the only thing that will get Jennings back on the fantasy football radar this year. Stay tuned. He had a career year in 2024 with San Francisco, posting a 77-975-6 line in 15 regular-season games, and he followed that up with a career-best nine touchdowns in 2025.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings - Doesn't catch only target Sunday
metadata.description: Jennings did not reel in his only target during Sunday's 23-13 win at New Orleans.
metadata.analysis: Jennings again got the second most snaps at wide receiver for the Vikings (47) in Week 5 with Jordan Addison (hamstring) out, but it only translated to one target on the afternoon. Jennings has failed to draw more than two targets in any game so far this season, and his role could be further diminished after Minnesota's bye in Week 6 if Addison is able to return to action.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings sees one target in Week 5
metadata.description: Jauan Jennings failed to catch his lone target in the Vikings' 23-13 Week 5 win over the New Orleans Saints.
metadata.analysis: Jennings has been a non-factor in the Minnesota passing attack to begin the season, finishing with two targets or less in each of his four games. The wideout can remain off rosters in all formats as the Vikings enter their bye week.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings Remains Off the Radar for Week 5
metadata.description: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings has handled a sizable snap share throughout the last two weeks, peaking with a 95% snap share in Week 4. Yet, he has continued to underperform on offense, catching just two passes across those two games. It has been disappointing to see him have so much trouble producing, especially given how much the Raiders are actively in search of an upgrade at the position. In other words, there was a direct path to production for Jennings, and he failed to seize it. With that being said, we don't expect much to change in Week 5 against the New Orleans Saints. The 29-year-old can be avoided in most fantasy leagues this week, due to both his season stats so far and the fact that New Orleans has ranked slightly stronger than league average in terms of receiving production allowed.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings Not a Priority Waiver Add for Week 5
metadata.description: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings got exactly the kind of opportunity fantasy managers were waiting for in Week 4, and almost nothing came of it. Justin Jefferson (ankle) was out, Kyler Murray attempted 37 passes, and Jennings finished with one catch for eight yards. T.J. Hockenson caught 13 passes for 119 yards and Jordan Addison added four catches for 52, which says plenty about where Jennings currently sits in this passing game. He now has only two receptions for nine yards in three appearances since joining Minnesota. Jefferson's status for Week 5 against New Orleans is still worth tracking, but even another absence would not make Jennings easy to trust after what happened Sunday. The Vikings also head into their bye immediately after this matchup. RotoBaller has Jennings down at WR74 in its early Week 5 half-PPR rankings. He is not a priority waiver add in standard leagues and is better left for deeper formats where managers can afford to wait for his role to change.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings - Remains quiet despite no Jefferson
metadata.description: Jennings caught his lone target for eight yards in Sunday's 15-10 win over the Dolphins.
metadata.analysis: Despite Justin Jefferson (ankle) missing Sunday's game, Jennings remained a non-factor on offense, as he took a distant back seat to all three of T.J. Hockenson, Jordan Addison and Aaron Jones. Jennings has two catches for nine yards on four targets across 152 offensive snaps through three games this season. He's well off the fantasy radar.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings held to one catch Sunday
metadata.description: Jauan Jennings caught just one pass for eight yards in Sunday's 15-10 win over the Miami Dolphins.
metadata.analysis: Jennings wasn't able to get much going on Sunday, finishing with just one catch in the team's win over Miami. He wasn't able to contribute even with Justin Jefferson (ankle) being out of the lineup for the Vikings, so he surely shouldn't be expected to produce when the star wideout is able to make his return to the lineup.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings - Opportunity boost likely Sunday
metadata.description: Jennings is in line to see a boost in targets as the Vikings' No. 2 receiver for Sunday's Week 4 matchup against the Dolphins, due to Justin Jefferson (hamstring) being ruled inactive for the contest.
metadata.analysis: Jennings' Vikings tenure has gotten off to an utterly forgettable start, as the veteran receiver has just one reception for one yard on three targets through two games. While Jennings was unable to capitalize on Jefferson's early exit from a Week 3 win over the Buccaneers, the former did log a season-high 47 snaps and ran 24 routes during the contest. Both numbers -- along with Jennings' target share -- will be in line to increase against Miami with Jefferson out, although the possibility Minnesota eventually has the luxury of turning to a run-heavy approach in the second half is also high considering the generally uncompetitive current state of the Dolphins.

metadata.title: Breakout Time For Jauan Jennings In Week 4?
metadata.description: It has been a quiet beginning of the season for Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings, but he could have a new opening when the team plays host to the Miami Dolphins now that star Vikings receiver Justin Jefferson (ankle) has been ruled out. The veteran receiver played 80% of offensive snaps last week after Jefferson departed, but the bigger issue is that the Vikings' passing game has struggled immensely. Minnesota ranks last in the NFL in net yards per attempt, though they face a Dolphins defense that has allowed points on half of opponents' possessions. The matchup looks great, and Jennings should see an uptick in snaps, but the state of the Vikings' passing offense is likely too risky for most formats until quarterback Kyler Murray clicks with his new team. Jennings has a pathway to more involvement, but as RotoBaller's No. 63 receiver this week, he's likely best saved for deeper formats.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings - Logs just one catch despite Jefferson injury
metadata.description: Jennings caught one of two targets for one yard Sunday in a 23-16 win against Tampa Bay.
metadata.analysis: Although Justin Jefferson (ankle) departed in the first half Sunday and didn't return, Jennings didn't see an increase in his production. He did, however, post an 80 percent offensive snap share, and Jennings figures to slide into the No. 2 wideout role alongside Jordan Addison on Sunday versus Miami if Jefferson can't suit up. Even with that in mind, Jennings has produced just one catch on three targets through two contests, so expectations should be held in check regardless of Jefferson's status.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings a Low-Priority Waiver Option Following Teammate's Injury
metadata.description: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings has caught only one pass for one yard since joining the team on a one-year free agent deal, but with four-time All-Pro Justin Jefferson (ankle) potentially sidelined, he could be thrust into a larger role. Jefferson left Sunday's win over the Buccaneers, and while initial reports indicate his ankle injury doesn't appear overly serious, his status will need to be monitored leading up to a Week 4 matchup with the Dolphins. In Jefferson's absence, Jordan Addison led the team with 90 yards and a touchdown on five catches, and he becomes a priority add wherever available, but Jennings should also see more involvement if Jefferson suffers a setback or misses time.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings catches one pass Sunday
metadata.description: Jauan Jennings caught 1-of-2 targets for one yard in the Vikings 23-16 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Jennings was unable to take advantage of the absence of Justin Jefferson (ankle) leaving early. He remains off the fantasy radar for now.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings - Back at practice
metadata.description: Jennings (personal) was not listed on the Vikings' injury report Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Jennings was unable to practice all week before ultimately sitting out Sunday's 9-3 win over the Bears while dealing with a personal matter. The 29-year-old returned to practice Wednesday, and he'll stand to operate as Minnesota's No. 3 option at wide receiver in the return of quarterback Kyler Murray against the Buccaneers in Week 3.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings (personal) good to go for Week 3
metadata.description: Jauan Jennings (personal) will be good to go for Week 3's matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
metadata.analysis: Jennings missed last week's game due to a personal issue that he was tending to, but he is back and fully good to go ahead of Minnesota's matchup against the Buccaneers in Week 3. He should play but isn't expected to be a relevant fantasy option for the foreseeable future.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings (personal) expected to return for Week 3
metadata.description: Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell said Jauan Jennings is expected to return for Week 3.
metadata.analysis: Jennings did not play on Sunday due to personal reasons. He was targeted just once in Week 1. He's off the fantasy radar for now.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings - Ruled out for Week 2
metadata.description: Jennings (not injury related - personal) won't play Sunday in Chicago.
metadata.analysis: Jennings didn't practice at all this week due to a personal matter and thus now has been ruled out for Week 2 action. The Vikings lean on Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison the most at wide receiver, but some targets seemingly will be available for Tai Felton and even Myles Price in Jennings' absence. Jennings' next chance to suit up will be Sunday, Sept. 27 at Tampa Bay.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings (personal) won't play Sunday
metadata.description: Jauan Jennings (personal) won't play in Sunday's game against the Chicago Bears.
metadata.analysis: The veteran wideout is going to be absent for Sunday's game. He is currently dealing with a personal issue of some kind, though the details of it are unknown at this point. Jordan Addison may see a little bit more work with Jennings out of the lineup.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings Ruled Out for Week 2
metadata.description: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings will not play Sunday against Chicago, head coach Kevin O'Connell said Friday, according to Matthew Coller. Jennings has been away from the team this week for a personal matter and did not practice Wednesday or Thursday. He had one target and no catches over 31 offensive snaps in his Vikings debut against Green Bay. Minnesota now has a hole to fill behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison. Myles Price is listed directly behind Jennings on the depth chart, while Tai Felton could also see more work. Neither played much on offense in the opener, logging three snaps apiece, so it isn't clear yet how the Vikings will divide Jennings' snaps.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings an Afterthought with New Team
metadata.description: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings (personal) belongs on the bench or waiver wire in all fantasy football leagues. Jennings played less than 50% of the snaps in Week 1, finishing with one target and zero receptions. It was a very disappointing appearance for the veteran receiver with his new team, especially after back-to-back top-33 fantasy finishes in San Francisco. This reduced role certainly didn't come out of nowhere, though. Jennings clearly entered the season as the No. 3 receiver behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, making it difficult for him to get onto the fantasy radar as long as those two pass-catchers stay healthy. To further complicate matters, Jennings missed practice Thursday due to a personal issue. Regardless of whether he suits up in Week 2 against the Bears, Jennings can be avoided in all leagues. He ranks as the WR79 in RotoBaller's Week 2 fantasy football rankings.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings (personal) absent from another practice Thursday
metadata.description: Jauan Jennings (personal) was absent from another practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: A personal issue of some kind left Jennings absent from a second-straight practice on Thursday. It's currently unclear whether or not it will affect his availability for Week 2, but he isn't fantasy relevant at this point in the season, so his injury status doesn't carry much weight for fantasy purposes.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings (personal) doesn't practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Jauan Jennings (personal) did not take part in Minnesota's practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran wideout was absent from Minnesota's practice on Wednesday due to a personal issue of some kind. It seems unlikely to affect his availability for Week 2, but he remains squarely off of the fantasy radar after going catchless in the season opener last week.

metadata.title: Jauan Jennings - Blanked in Minnesota debut
metadata.description: Jennings did not bring in his lone target during the Vikings' 39-22 win over the Packers on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Kyler Murray's first pass attempt of the game was to Jennings, resulting in a Kiesean Nixon interception that led to a 59-yard field goal from Trey Smack six plays later. Jennings didn't see another pass the rest of the way, even after Carson Wentz took over as the Vikings QB for Murray after the former left the game due to a concussion. Jennings' 31 snaps on offense were third-most among wide receivers behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, but the lack of offensive output from Jennings was disappointing given the solid production he had with the 49ers in 2024 and 2025. He'll look for better results in the Vikings' Week 2 clash Sept. 20, against a Bears defense that gave up 361 passing yards to Bryce Young in a 59-37 Week 1 win for Chicago.
